newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: S. America blocs call for single free-trade zone.
newsitem.headline: S. America blocs call for single free-trade zone.

text.p: South America's two main trade blocs, Mercosur and the Andean Community, on Wednesday said they want to form a single free-trade area.

The presidents of the Andean nations -- Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela -- signed a joint declaration calling for the formation of a new free-trade area along with the president of Paraguay, representing Mercosur.

The document, issued at a meeting of the presidents in Bolivia's official capital, declared "the firm political will...to speed up the technical work to allow the formation of a free-trade zone as soon as possible."

Paraguay's partners in the Mercosur customs union are South America's two largest economies, Brazil and Argentina, as well as Uruguay. Like Chile, Bolivia has already signed a free-trade agreement with Mercosur.
